results.summary: This design generates a 640x480 VGA video signal showing a rocket animation. It uses a standard VGA sync generator with 800 pixels per line and 525 lines per frame, producing a 59.94 Hz refresh rate at a 25.175 MHz pixel clock. The project requires a VGA Pmod connected to a monitor that supports 640x480 @ 59.94 Hz. The demo is not interactive; the user simply waits to see if the animation appears.

This project is a Verilog-based game that renders output to a VGA screen and includes PWM audio output. It uses custom AI implemented in HDL, as indicated by the description. The design is controlled by eight input pins labeled as gamepad buttons (Up, Down, Left, Right, A, B, Select, Start). It requires a VGA display and optionally an audio Pmod, similar to the VGA Playground setup.

This ASIC implements a low-power pedometer that processes 48-bit SPI frames from an ADXL345 or MPU6050 MEMS accelerometer. It computes the magnitude of the 3-axis acceleration using the Alpha-Max Beta-Min algorithm and detects steps via threshold crossing with hysteresis and a gait regularity filter. The step count is output on eight pins, and a byte select pin allows reading the count in bytes. The design operates at 32.768 kHz and consumes only 656 nW, making it suitable for ultra-low-power applications.

This design is a VGA demo that simulates a Galton peg board with falling paint balls that create a histogram of landing positions. It uses three prime LFSR sequences to generate random left/right decisions at each peg, and the balls squish at the bottom. The design supports optional gamepad and audio Pmods for interactive control and sound effects. It can also be controlled via simple input pins when no gamepad is present.

This project implements the classic game Pong on raw silicon, generating VGA video and stereo audio. It uses a custom VGA sync module and pixel-clock-based logic to render sprites and background colors. The game is controlled by six buttons for two players (up, down, serve for each). External hardware includes a TinyVGA Pmod and buttons with pull-down resistors.

This design implements an 8-bit posit multiply-accumulate (MAC) unit with a 32-bit quire register for exact accumulation. It takes two 8-bit posit inputs (es=2), multiplies them, and accumulates the product into the quire, which can be read back as a posit8 or cleared. The unit uses ready/valid handshaking and is controlled via a finite state machine, with data read/written through bidirectional ports. It is tested with a testbench that verifies basic operations, accumulation, and dot product fuzz testing against a float reference.

This project implements the PRESENT block cipher with a hardware trojan that can inject faults. It has an 8-bit data input, 8-bit data output, and command inputs via bidirectional pins. The design is tested with functional tests from OpenCores and additional tests for encryption rounds with fixed key and plaintext to verify fault behavior. The hardware trojan is a deliberate malicious modification, making this a security research project.

This circuit is a Verilog quine that outputs its own source code as a 640x480 VGA image. It uses a bitmap font to render the source code, which is stored in a hexadecimal array, and displays it on a VGA monitor. The design takes no input and must be clocked at 25.175 MHz. It is notable for being the first Verilog quine to output via VGA and the first hardened quine.

This analog design implements a true random number generator based on a current-starved ring oscillator. It has four analog pins: VCTRL for control voltage, XORCHAIN for XOR feedback, FOUT for frequency output, and CLK for clock input. The design is intended to produce truly random sequences of ones and zeros. The documentation is essentially absent, providing only the title and pin names, so the exact operation and testing method are not described.

This design is a demo for the ttsky26a competition, featuring an LFSR starfield background and a cellular automata monolith in the foreground, with a TT logo sticker from ROM. It plays a 2001: A Space Odyssey inspired theme via PWM audio. The design outputs VGA video at 800x600 @ ~56.35 Hz and requires a 36 MHz clock. External hardware includes a VGA Pmod and an Audio Pmod.
